A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Shape of Motion and retain matching methods, experiments and visualizations. The complete text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes Appendices A-G.

before.justification: v1 reports original iPhone tracking and view-synthesis experiments, Kubric tracking results, and component ablations in Tables 1-3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds NVIDIA results, additional comparator and model-variant results, an ablation, and a DAVIS visualization.

M1.justification: The shared SE(3) motion-basis representation and trajectory rendering remain. v2 adds an optional 2DGS variant with monocular-normal supervision (Appendix B.2), and introduces MegaSaM initialization followed by joint camera-pose refinement for in-the-wild videos (Section 3.3). These extend the retained reconstruction method.

E1.justification: Alongside the retained iPhone and Kubric evaluations, v2 adds novel-view synthesis on seven NVIDIA scenes captured from a static training camera. Appendix E also adds a qualitative multi-object DAVIS school-girl example. This materially broadens the evaluated data and capture conditions.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds DynMF, DELTA (world), and SpatialTracker (world) to the iPhone comparison while retaining the previous comparators. New Table 3 evaluates Dynamic Gaussian Marbles on NVIDIA. DynMF and Dynamic Gaussian Marbles were already cited in v1 but were not evaluated there.

E3.justification: The stated motion-basis count changes from 20 to 10. The new NVIDIA protocol trains on camera 4 and evaluates cameras 3, 5 and 6 at half resolution using covisibility masks (Appendix F). Added frame-space tracking baselines are transformed into world coordinates. These introduce substantive experimental settings; retained numerical results do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a Per-Gaussian SE(3) ablation to isolate the contribution of shared motion bases, alongside the 2DGS variant comparison and a qualitative DAVIS case study. Existing ablations remain. The Kubric PCA visualization is relocated to Appendix D, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. TAPIR uncertainty scores used during optimization concern input confidence, not statistical uncertainty of the reported experimental results.

E6.justification: Original iPhone, Kubric and retained ablation scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial result entries. Its 2DGS variant reports EPE 0.097 versus 0.082 for the original model, while LPIPS improves from 0.45 to 0.40. NVIDIA mean PSNR is 23.37 for Ours versus 23.46 for DGM. Reported rendering speed changes from approximately 40 to 140 FPS, without sufficient timing details to establish a controlled speedup.

T1.justification: Equation 7 changes the mask-loss target from constant 1 to the input mask M, correcting the formal objective to match the stated supervision. Appendix B.2 introduces normal-supervision loss definitions for the 2DGS variant. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim joint persistent 3D tracking and novel-view synthesis through compact SE(3) motion bases and consolidation of learned priors, with state-of-the-art performance. v2 emphasizes world-coordinate trajectories, but that capability was already specified in v1. The main contribution scope is retained.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds a three-part explanation of gains over TAPIR+DA involving shared motion, acceleration regularization and persistent geometry. The limitations discussion broadens dependence on external predictions to geometry and motion and discusses newer alternatives. However, v1's explicit inability to handle large viewpoint changes is omitted without evidence that it was resolved.

D1.justification: New appendices substantially document preprocessing, track sampling and filtering, learning rates, loss weights, batching, regularization, metric-scale alignment and the DynMF implementation. These mostly expand documentation of the retained pipeline. A reproducibility inconsistency remains: v2's main text specifies 1000 initialization iterations, whereas Appendix B.1 specifies 2000 steps.

R1.justification: v2 substantially updates positioning through classical low-rank reconstruction and newer learned reconstruction and tracking work, including DELTA, SpatialTracker, DUSt3R and MonST3R. It replaces v1's absence-of-generic-3D-trackers rationale with a distinction between frame-space and world-space trajectories, and discusses newer joint reconstruction/tracking and motion-segmentation approaches.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the method exposition remain. v2 selectively condenses and rewrites the abstract, introduction, baseline descriptions and discussion, makes world-coordinate terminology more explicit, updates authors and affiliations, and organizes additional documentation into appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with widespread resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. Figure 1 moves onto the title page, Figure 6 moves to the appendix, Table 1 and the ablation table gain rows, and a NVIDIA results table and DAVIS Figure 7 are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens reproducibility and empirical assessment through detailed appendices, relevant additional competitors, a direct shared-basis ablation and a distinct static-camera evaluation. The new results expose useful performance tradeoffs while retaining the original evidence. The conflicting initialization budgets and removal of the large-viewpoint limitation temper these gains, but the improved methodological transparency and stronger comparisons provide a substantial net improvement.
